title: Your Relationship After Baby
hook: A new baby tests even strong relationships. Sharing the load, talking honestly, and working as a team — while expecting routines and intimacy to shift for a while — helps you weather it together.
key_points: New parenthood strains even loving relationships; the stress is normal, not a sign something's wrong with you two.
Share the load — feedings, diapers, night shifts, and household tasks — so neither partner carries it all.
Communicate needs and work as a team; a strong partnership helps the whole family adjust.
Expect intimacy and routines to change for a while; small affection like cuddling keeps you connected.
content_html: A new baby reshapes your days — and your relationship. Even strong, loving partnerships feel the strain of sleepless nights, new responsibilities, and less time together, and that stress is normal rather than a sign something is wrong between you.
extra_html: The AAP encourages partners to share the load: trade off diaper changes, feedings, calming the baby, and household tasks, since even a few extra hours of sleep helps both parents cope. Support the birthing parent in concrete ways, communicate your needs, and approach early parenthood as a team — children tend to adjust better when their parents have a strong, loving relationship. Expect intimacy and routines to change for a while, and stay connected through small gestures like cuddling and snuggling. Make a little time for each other when you can, and don't hesitate to ask for and accept help. This is general guidance; if you or your partner notice persistent low mood or anxiety, reach out to your doctor.

related.title: You Can't Pour From an Empty Cup
related.hook: Looking after yourself isn't a luxury — it's part of caring for your baby. A rested, supported parent has more patience and presence to give.

related.title: Baby Blues or Something More?
related.hook: Weepy and overwhelmed in the first days is common and usually passes within two weeks. When low mood lingers and disrupts daily life, it may be postpartum depression — common and treatable.

flashcards.prompt: How can partners share the load after a new baby arrives?

choices.text: Trade off feedings, diapers, night shifts, and household tasks
Leave all baby care to the birthing parent
Wait until the baby is older to help out

flashcards.explanation_html: The AAP recommends partners take shifts with diapers, feedings, calming the baby, and chores — even a few extra hours of sleep helps both parents cope.

flashcards.prompt: Is it normal for intimacy and routines to change after a baby?
flashcards.back_html: Yes. Intimacy and daily routines shift for a while after a baby. Staying connected through small affection — cuddling, snuggling — helps keep the bond strong.

flashcards.prompt: What does the AAP say about the strain a new baby puts on a relationship?

choices.text: It's a normal stress, eased by teamwork and communication
A strong couple won't feel any strain
Strain means the relationship is failing

flashcards.explanation_html: New parenthood strains even loving relationships. Sharing duties, communicating, and making time for each other help the whole family adjust.
